Satisfies REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE and REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER (clear placeholders and guidance) and REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE (no guessing of real IDs/paths). - insertSupportsTemplate(fixer, sourceCode, customTemplate?): - Determines insertIndex at file start, but after a shebang if present to preserve executable semantics. - Calls fixer.insertTextBeforeRange([insertIndex, insertIndex], templateComment). - Only adds a comment; no test code modification → supports REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE and REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE. - ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, autoFixOptions): - Scans all comments for @supports; if found, does nothing (avoids duplicates). - If missing, reports messageId: "missingFileSupports". - Provides fix only when autoFixOptions.autoFixTestTemplate !== false, using insertSupportsTemplate with optional testSupportsTemplate override. - JSDoc @supports for Story 021.0 lists REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE.,Helper implementation – src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts (REQ prefix normalization): - normalizeReqId(raw: string): - Trims and uppercases; requires leading "REQ". - Drops leading separators after REQ, converts whitespace/underscores to hyphens, collapses multiple hyphens. - Returns canonical REQ-... string without inventing new semantics → implements REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT and respects REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE. - normalizeReqPrefixInDescription(description: string): - If canonical pattern /^\[REQ-[^\]]+]/ already matches, returns null (no fix) → preserves correct cases. - Handles malformed forms: - "[ REQ-XXX ]..." via squareMatch → "[REQ-XXX]..." (spacing fix). - "[REQ_XXX]..." → "[REQ-XXX]..." (underscore → hyphen). - "(REQ-XXX)..." → "[REQ-XXX]..." (parentheses → square brackets). - "[req-xxx]..." → "[REQ-XXX]..." (case normalization). - Returns null if no REQ-like match at the start; no fix is emitted, satisfying REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE and REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE. - createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw(originalNode, newValue, sourceCode): - Reads raw source text, preserves original quote style (' / " / `) and escapes embedded quotes and backslashes. - Only changes literal content, not surrounding code → supports REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE. - handleItOrTestCall(context, node, description, options): - Applies only when requireTestReqPrefix is true. - If description does not start with canonical [REQ-...]: - If autoFixTestPrefixFormat !== false, calls normalizeReqPrefixInDescription. - Always reports messageId: "missingReqPrefix". - Only attaches a fix when: - autoFixTestPrefixFormat !== false, - normalizedDescription !== null, - first argument is a string Literal. - Fix replaces only the literal using createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw. - This ensures: malformed-but-recognizable prefixes are normalized (REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE), and absent/ambiguous prefixes cause errors with **no fix** (REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE).,Visitor wiring – src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts: - handleCallExpression(context, options) returns a CallExpression visitor that: - Uses getCalleeName and isTestCallName to handle describe/it/test/context only (REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT dependency from Story 020.0). - For describe: delegates to handleDescribeCall (validation only; no auto-fix here, matching story’s OUT OF SCOPE for adding story references). - For it/test: delegates to handleItOrTestCall, which performs malformed-prefix normalization as described above. - This aligns with the story’s Implementation Notes (auto-fix only for missing file-level @supports and malformed [REQ-XXX] prefixes, not for describe story references or adding new prefixes).,Tests – tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts (traceability and coverage): - File header JSDoc: - @supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE explicitly links this test file to Story 021.0 and all its requirements. - Valid cases: - A case with already-correct [REQ-TRACE-123] name and proper @supports confirms that correctly-formatted prefixes are left unchanged, supporting REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE and REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE. - Invalid cases (auto-fix and safety): - File-level template insertion (REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE): - Input code: describe('Story 020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION', () => { it('[REQ-ONE] works', () => {}); }); - Expected output in test: /** * @supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ * TODO: Replace the placeholder story path and REQ-IDs with real values for this test file. */ describe(...) - Confirms ESLint’s fixer inserts the placeholder JSDoc at the top, with clear TODO text, and leaves the test body unchanged. - No REQ prefix (REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE, Error Handling): - Code has valid @supports but it('missing prefix', ...) without any [REQ-...] prefix. - Test expects errors: [{ messageId: "missingReqPrefix" }] and no output field (no auto-fix), proving the rule reports but **does not invent** a requirement prefix. - Malformed prefix normalization (REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE): - Spacing: '[ REQ-TEST-FIX ] does something' → '[REQ-TEST-FIX] does something'. - Underscore: '[REQ_TEST_FIX] does something' → '[REQ-TEST-FIX] does something'. - Lowercase: '[req-lowercase] bad casing' → '[REQ-LOWERCASE] bad casing'. - Parentheses: '(REQ-PAREN) with parens' → '[REQ-PAREN] with parens'. - All tests specify both input code and expected output strings, verifying exactly the transformations described in the story’s Implementation Notes.,Test execution (project-wide): - Command previously run in this session: npm test -- --runInBand --verbose - Output excerpt: - PASS tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts require-test-traceability rule (Stories 020.0 and 021.0) valid ✓ /** @supports ...021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT */ describe('Story 021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX', () => { it('[REQ-TRACE-123] behaves correctly', () => {}); traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and requirements for docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md are implemented and verified: - File-level @supports template insertion is implemented via ensureFileSupportsAnnotation and insertSupportsTemplate, using a placeholder JSDoc block with explicit TODO guidance (REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER) and never inferring real story paths or IDs (REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE). - Malformed [REQ-XXX] prefixes in test names are normalized for spacing, underscores, case, and parentheses via normalizeReqId and normalizeReqPrefixInDescription, only when a recognizable REQ ID is already present (REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE). - String literal rewriting preserves quote style and escapes, and only comments or test name prefixes are changed, preserving test behavior and structure (REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE and Quality Standards). - The functionality is integrated into the ESLint rule with meta.fixable: "code" and configurable options autoFixTestTemplate, autoFixTestPrefixFormat, and testSupportsTemplate, and is exercised via RuleTester tests that specify before/after code for all auto-fix scenarios. - Jest test suite (including tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts) passes, confirming the behavior works end-to-end, and user-facing documentation in user-docs/api-reference.md clearly describes these auto-fix capabilities and options.
Based on this concrete code, tests, and documentation, the story is fully implemented and passes all acceptance criteria and Definition of Done items.
